findings.finding: S03-queue-layer/spec.md does not exist at the pinned commit 56b9cf1, yet the spec cites it twice: the header's section-numbering note ('S03-queue-layer/spec.md cites this document's §2.1, §2.5 and §3') and §4.2 ('ordering is S03's concern (S03-queue-layer/spec.md §2.1)'). The file was committed only in 08bc2d5, which is a descendant of the pin. The spec's own pinning rule (header: 'A citation that no longer resolves at 56b9cf1 is a spec defect') is violated for this §ref; the header's in-flight note names three dirty files but not S03. It resolves in the current tree (S03's Inputs cite pass2 §2.1/§3/§2.5; line 903 cites §2.1/§2.4/§2.5/§3), so the substance is accurate today.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT (partial). Either pin the S03 §ref to the commit where S03 exists, or add S03-queue-layer/spec.md to the header's in-flight note alongside the three dirty files. No line-numbered citation is taken from S03, so the F11 discipline holds for file:line; the gap is §ref-existence pinning.

findings.finding: §3.1's launch-template family set {deepseek, claude, ollama} and §4's appetite-dial family set {claude, claude-fable, deepseek, ollama-cloud, local} are two taxonomies wearing the same word 'family', and no label→family mapping is specified. The ollama row's four labels span two dial families (glm-5.2/minimax-m3/kimi-k2.7 → ollama-cloud; qwen3.8:27b-mlx → local per measurement-methodology.md §1 'local (qwen / gemma)'); the claude row's labels span claude and claude-fable (the 200k boundary). 'local' has no launch-template row at all. Since §4's lane cap, spacing and hard-forbid are keyed per dial family, the appetite gate cannot be enforced as specified until the mapping exists; arm D6's synthetic 4th row does not name its dial family.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Add a per-row appetite-family column (or a label→family rule) to the §3.1 table and pin the correspondence; have D6 name the synthetic row's dial family. Without it the builder must invent the mapping, and two builders would invent two.

findings.finding: RUN-4's replicant check collides on (holds, justification-key), but 'justification-key' is undefined. RUN-3 defines justification as 'non-empty free text'; no normalization or structured key is specified, so arm R5 (a stub minting 'an exact copy of its own row (same holds, same justification key)') cannot be built as written, and the cheapest of the five runaway defenses is unmechanizable.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Define the key: either a structured justification schema with a stable key field, or an explicit normalization rule over the free text (the justification field itself is the one thing a replicating worker controls, so the key definition is load-bearing).

findings.finding: RUN-1's Δ observation channel is unpinned. 'On every close the supervisor records Δ = open(after) − open(before)' — but the section's own preamble states 'a worker can write the store directly (managent add)', and a worker can also close its own row directly; the supervisor is not the only closer. Whether Δ is accumulated at the store write (under the lock, consistent with the section's 'enforced at the store write' thesis) or sampled from the supervisor's poll view is unspecified, and the two disagree for direct worker closes. Arms R1/R1-null pass under either reading, so they do not discriminate.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Pin Δ accumulation to the store write path (the write is already serialized by the store lock, so the derivative is exact), or state the supervisor's observation window and what a direct-worker close does to the count.

findings.finding: No grandfathering rule for pre-pass-2 store rows. At 56b9cf1 the live queue holds ~30 rows with no minted_by/lineage/justification; RUN-2/3's write-time rejection would make them undispatchable after the change, or silently exempt — the spec says neither. There is also an unresolved tension inside RUN-2: 'a row written with zero authors (an anonymous mint) ... is rejected at write time', while RUN-3 says an operator-added row is authorless by design ('A row an operator adds has lineage = [self]'). The caller-identity distinction at the store write is never stated (only §4.4's worker marker, and only for the appetite verb).
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. State the operator-vs-worker distinction at the store write (reuse the §4.4 marker: MANAGENT_TASK_ID / held-child marker) and the legacy-row migration (e.g., lineage=[self] + operator authorship backfilled at cutover, or the checks scoped to rows created after the cutover).

findings.finding: DP-6's gate scan scope is under-specified. Predicate (i) — 'a file outside it holding ≥ 2 labels is a FAIL' — does not state which paths are scanned, whether comment lines are stripped, or whether data files are excluded. The naive raw-grep reading is red on the shipped tree at the pin: tools/suite-truth.sh (4 label mentions, all provenance comments), tools/bakeoff-dryrun.roster (data file, 2), src/t394_force_life.zig and src/vb_bellman_4x4.zig (instruments emitting their own task/model identity into JSON output, 2 code hits each). The measured 'seven non-test files' enumeration holds only under an unstated code-only, comment-stripped reading; D5-null's green assertion is undefined until the scope is pinned.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. State the scan rule: reuse DP-3's comment stripping (grep -v '^[[:space:]]*//'), scope to non-test code files, exclude data by extension (roster/json/jsonl), and name the self-identifying-instrument exception (a file whose label literals occur only in its own identity emission) or accept them as pinned allowlist entries.

findings.finding: The spec misquotes the seed's pass numbering for the deferred run-record migration: §1.1, §9 and the changelog F2 row all call it 'the seed's Pass 5', but the seed (docs/status/refactor-roadmap-2026-08-20.md:144, :161) assigns Pass 3 to 'run records and heartbeats into the store' and Pass 5 to the supervisor itself — the very pass this spec builds. The misnumbering originates in audit-disposition F2's wording and was carried into rev-2. The deferral substance is correct and honestly stated; the label collides with the name of the pass being implemented, so a reader can misread the spec as deferring part of its own deliverable. scope.md's Won't row ('run-records-into-store (seed Pass 3)') already has it right.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT. Correct to 'the seed's Pass 3' in §1.1, §9 and the changelog F2 row. Trivial edit; the collision is the only harm.

findings.finding: §4.5's migration table lists ollama-cloud's 'old level' as SPEND with dial 90, but measurement-methodology.md §1 at the pin records the family as 'OFF → SPEND', 0 tokens, ~48h window, 'rejoin is a human flip, never a calendar auto-trust' — the recorded state is OFF pending a human flip, which is not 'SPEND' and makes a default of 90 sit above the methodology's recorded state. The spec explicitly flags all §4.5 numbers as operator-unratified (§11 Q6, 'operator to ratify the numbers'), so this is a mapping-accuracy note, not a mechanism defect.
findings.disposition: ACCEPT (note). When the operator ratifies the dial numbers, the ollama-cloud default should be reconciled with the methodology's human-flip OFF state; the mapping claim ('the numbers are the operator's') is already the correct framing.
